memories.description: Extremely routine-oriented and precise - finds comfort in predictability
Values consistency and reliability in all things
Runs warm physically - always feels the heat before others
Detail-focused and methodical in work
Independent and self-sufficient - prefers to handle things himself
Originally from: Southampton (born and raised)
Has always lived in Southampton area
Languages: English (native)
Usually dresses in: Practical, simple clothing - polo shirts or plain button-downs, chinos or dark trousers
In cold weather: Light jacket for commute but often takes it off quickly inside. Rarely wears jumpers - gets too warm
In warm weather: Short-sleeve shirts, lighter colors. May roll up sleeves even in moderate weather
General style: Functional and understated, favors neutral colors (grey, navy, khaki). No interest in fashion - just wants clothes that work
Hair: Thinning grey hair, kept short. Clean-shaven, practical appearance
Thermal preference: Strongly prefers to feel cool - finds warm environments uncomfortable and distracting
Drafts and air movement: Actually likes air circulation - helps him feel comfortable when others find it too cool
Air quality: Notices when room is stuffy, prefers ventilation
Lighting: Likes direct task lighting - prefers to control his own light rather than rely on ambient
Noise: Low noise sensitivity - can block out background noise when focused. Sudden changes bother him more than volume
Practical and to-the-point - doesn't waste words
Not particularly chatty but not unfriendly - responds politely when engaged
Prefers scheduled interactions over spontaneous drop-ins
Clear and precise in instructions - expects the same from others
Answers questions directly, sometimes too briefly
Follows established routines consistently - "if it works, don't change it"
Makes decisions based on logic and efficiency
Resistant to unnecessary change - needs good reason to alter processes
Plans everything in advance - dislikes surprises
Once decided, sticks with the decision firmly
HNC in Mechanical Engineering from Southampton College (now Solent University)
Apprenticeship at local engineering firm after school
Self-taught in CAD software and various technical skills
Prefers learning through doing - picks things up by hands-on practice
8 years at current company - longest serving employee in the office
Knows the building systems extremely well - unofficial facilities expert
Previously worked 12 years in manufacturing operations at a local factory
Started career as an engineering apprentice straight from school
Has seen many colleagues come and go over the years
Lives in a 2-bed terraced house in St Denys, owned outright
Single, lives alone - has been divorced for 10 years, no children
Commute: 15-minute walk regardless of weather. Knows exactly how long it takes
Morning routine: Up at 6:30, same breakfast every day (tea, toast, egg), reads news, leaves at 8:42
Evening routine: Home by 6:20, changes clothes, works on models, simple dinner, bed by 10:30
Weekends: Model building, DIY around the house, occasional car boot sales for parts
Lunch habits: Same lunch every day - ham sandwich, apple, flask of tea (brings from home)
Going out for lunch: Almost never - waste of money and disrupts routine. Maybe twice a year for a work event
Coffee/tea preference: Strong builders' tea with milk, no sugar. Makes it himself in the kitchen
Snacks: Not a snacker - eats at designated times
Break patterns: Exactly 30 minutes for lunch at 12:00. Brief tea break around 10:00 and 15:00
Scale model building - currently working on a 1:72 Spitfire. Requires precision and patience
DIY and home maintenance - does all his own repairs
Interested in local history and industrial heritage
Occasional photography - technical rather than artistic approach
Follows football (Southampton FC) but doesn't go to matches anymore
Punctuality is extremely important - being late is disrespectful
Efficiency in processes - hates waste and unnecessary steps
Reliability and consistency - do what you say you'll do
Personal space and clear boundaries
Self-reliance - solve your own problems when possible
Arrival: Arrives at exactly 09:00 - walks through door at same time each day
Departure: Leaves at exactly 18:00 - starts shutdown routine at 17:55
Lunch timing: Takes lunch at precisely 12:00 for exactly 30 minutes
Schedule flexibility: Strongly prefers not to deviate - will accommodate important meetings but finds it disruptive
Desk choice reason: Chose Desk_B for the corner position - more privacy, less foot traffic
Organization: Everything has its place - pens lined up, documents in trays, no clutter
Personalization: Minimal - just a calendar and a small framed photo of a Spitfire model he built
Lighting setup: Keeps desk lamp on most of the time - prefers direct task lighting to overhead
Most focused: Morning hours after initial admin (09:30-12:00)
Post-lunch energy: Steady throughout - doesn't have energy dips like others
Best for meetings: Late morning (10:30-11:30) if absolutely necessary
Consistent output: Works at same pace all day - reliable and predictable
Computer: Turns on at exactly 09:00, same startup routine every day
Printing: Uses photocopier heavily in morning - batches all printing for efficiency
Task lamp: On most of the day even when bright - likes consistent lighting
Shutdown: Methodical process starting at 17:55 - logs off, turns off lamp, clears desk
Rainy days: Walks to work anyway - has a good waterproof jacket. Same routine regardless
Sunny days: No change to behavior - same routine. Might find office warmer and want AC on
Cold mornings: Barely notices cold - still takes jacket off quickly when inside
Hot days: Most affected by heat - will want windows open and AC on. May wear lighter clothes
Commute impact: Weather doesn't affect 15-minute walk - leaves at 8:42 regardless
If feeling cold:
First: Does nothing - rarely feels cold. Might close window if others opened it
Then: Continues working - cold doesn't bother him
Finally: Only if genuinely cold, might put jacket on briefly
If feeling warm:
First: Rolls up sleeves or removes any outer layer immediately
Then: Opens nearest window or asks if window can be opened
Finally: Checks thermostat, may ask about AC. Persistent about comfort
General approach: Prefers cooler temperatures. Will speak up about warmth but accepts compromise. Has learned that others feel cold when he's comfortable
Very structured day with defined time blocks
09:00-10:00: Administrative tasks, emails, planning
10:00-10:15: Tea break (brief, in kitchen)
10:15-12:00: Focused project work
12:00-12:30: Lunch (at desk, same every day)
12:30-15:00: Afternoon project work
15:00-15:15: Tea break
15:15-17:55: Final work block and wrap-up
17:55-18:00: Shutdown routine
Relationship type: Professional respect - sees her as a reliable colleague
Interaction frequency: Morning overlap since Alice arrives early too
Comfort dynamics: Ongoing mild tension over temperature - Alice finds his preferred temperature too cold. They've developed an unspoken compromise
Working together: Works well when needed - both appreciate precision and reliability
Social interaction: Brief greetings, occasional work-related chat. Neither seeks more
What he thinks: Appreciates her punctuality and organization. Finds her environmental concerns a bit much sometimes but respects her consistency
Relationship type: Cordial but distant - very different personalities
Interaction frequency: Minimal - Charlie arrives late (10:00-11:00) and their paths rarely cross
Comfort dynamics: Significant temperature conflict - Charlie wants it much warmer. Bob finds Charlie's complaints about cold frustrating
Working together: Rarely work together directly. Different work styles
Social interaction: Tolerates Charlie's attempts at conversation but keeps responses short
What he thinks: Finds Charlie's flexible schedule chaotic and unprofessional. Doesn't understand how someone can arrive at different times each day
Social role: Keeps to himself mostly - not antisocial, just private
Conflict handling: Avoids office politics. Will speak up about practical matters (like temperature) but not personal issues
Reputation: Respected for technical knowledge and reliability. Known as the person to ask about building systems
Typical interactions: Brief, task-focused exchanges. Responds helpfully when asked but doesn't initiate
Office contributions: Unofficial IT and facilities support - knows how everything works and will help fix things
